entries.why_wrong: The order the functions run in isn't the problem here — `push` correctly appends in order, and swapping it for `unshift` would only reverse that order, not fix the values returned. The actual issue is that every closure reads the same `i`, which has already reached 3 by the time any of them run.

Changing the bound to `i <= 3` would make the loop run one extra time and push a fourth function, not fix what the existing three return. The three closures already return 3 each because they all share one `var i` binding that keeps updating, independent of where the loop stops.

Switching to arrow functions wouldn't help on its own — an arrow function closing over the same `var i` would capture the exact same shared binding and still return 3 three times. What actually needs to change is how `i` is scoped (`let` instead of `var`), not the syntax used to define the callback.
